name: Sanders Park Campground
note: Racine County park, 4703 Wood Rd, Mt Pleasant; 19-site campground, largest sites fit a 45-ft rig; fire pit & picnic table per site, no on-site dump (may use Cliffside dump); reservations required; season 2nd weekend Apr-2nd weekend Oct. --Claude

name: Victoria Riverside Park and Campground
note: Village of Muscoda city park on the Wisconsin River (Grant County); 45 electric campsites plus 16 seasonal full-hookup (electric/water/sewer) sites and a primitive tent area; boat launch (2 ramps), bathhouse w/ showers, dump station; reservable by phone/email; season ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Muskego Park
note: Waukesha County park on a swimming/fishing pond W of Muskego. 17 family sites (9 electric) + 3 group sites; beach, hiking. Reservable online via county system, open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Bay Shore Park Campground
note: Brown County park (RV Life mis-tagged commercial) on the W shore of Green Bay, ~15 mi NE of Green Bay on WI-57. ~117 wooded sites: 85 W/E, 30 rustic, 2 group; asphalt pads, showers, dump, boat launch. FCFS + online reservations, open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Holtwood Campground
note: City of Oconto park, 68 acres with ~4,000 ft frontage on the Oconto River, 30 min N of Green Bay. 152 sites (15/30/50A) + 9 primitive; showers, laundry, dump/pump-out, store, boat launch. Takes nightly transients + seasonal. Open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Hines Park Campground
note: City of Park Falls park on the E bank of the N Fork Flambeau River, within city limits. 9 paved full-hookup sites (W/S, 20/30/50A) fitting RVs 45+ ft + adjacent tent area; 2 fishing piers, boat launch, playground. FCFS, not reservable, open May-early Oct. --Claude

name: Peshtigo Badger Park Campground
note: City of Peshtigo park; 42-site campground in the SW portion of the 60-acre park along ~3,000 ft of Peshtigo River frontage. 35 RV sites with water+electric, 2 cabins, 4 rustic tent sites, 1 group site; showers/flush toilets, dump station. Open ~May-Oct, reservable online (Firefly). ~$27/night. --Claude

name: Cliffside County Park
note: Racine County park (233 acres) in the Village of Caledonia, 7320 Michna Rd. 92 back-in sites, all with electric + water, accommodating rigs to ~45 ft; dump station, showers, playfields. Open ~2nd weekend of April-Oct 31. Half the sites (1-41) held for walk-ins FCFS; rest reservable online via Real Racine (~7 days ahead, $12 res fee). --Claude

name: Hoffman Park Campground
note: City of River Falls campground. 15 RV sites with electric (rigs to ~43 ft) plus 5 grass tent sites; restrooms, showers, water fill, dump station. No campfires permitted. Open ~April 15-Oct 15. Reservable online (electric $25, tent $15; full prepayment required), camp host on site. --Claude

name: Collins Park
note: Portage County park (21 wooded acres) ~3 mi SW of Rosholt, next to 42-acre Collins Lake. ~27-28 campsites, all with electric ($8/night add-on); picnic lodge, boat ramp, showers, dump station, small swimming beach. Open ~May 15-Sep 30. About half the sites reservable online (7 days-11 months ahead), rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Shawano Lake County Park Campground
note: Shawano County Parks, W5785 N Lake Dr, Shawano. ~100 sites — 91-92 with water and 50-amp electric (no sewer), 8 tent-only electric sites, 1 ADA site; dump station, showers, ~800 ft of Shawano Lake shoreline with sand beach and boat launch. Open ~May-Oct; reservable online up to 12 months ahead. --Claude

name: Beauford T. Anderson Campground
note: Operated by the Village of Soldiers Grove (Crawford County); 35 electric+water sites plus tent camping, dump station, showers; big rigs and pull-thrus noted. FCFS, no reservations - passes bought at the Village Office or Campbell's One Stop. Season opens late April. Electric $25, non-electric $23/night. On the Kickapoo River. --Claude

name: Lucius Woods County Park
note: Douglas County Forestry-operated county park on Upper St. Croix Lake at Solon Springs (despite the 'State Park' name in some directories, it is a Douglas County park). ~32 sites: 23 electric/water, 9 non-electric; showers, flush toilets, dump station, swimming beach. Season ~two Fridays before Memorial Day to after Labor Day; reservable online (PremierCampground) starting Feb 1, $5 reservation fee. Electric $25, electric+water $30, non-electric $20/night. --Claude

name: Otter Lake County Park
note: Chippewa County Parks-operated park in the Chippewa County Forest, ~7.5 mi north of Stanley (35337 170th Ave). 22 drive-in sites, all with 20/30/50-amp electric; 15 sites have their own boat dock. Fill station on-site (sanitary dump shared via Chapman Park in Stanley). Season ~first week of May to late October; reservable online through mid-Sept, FCFS self-registration thereafter. $20/night + $7 electric + $5 dock site. --Claude

name: Stockholm Village Park Campground
note: Village of Stockholm park campground on Lake Pepin (Mississippi River). 23 sites with 50-amp electric (count reduced during high water); no water hookup at sites (potable water on-site, arrive with tank filled). Privy toilets, swimming beach, boat ramp, 700' fishing pier. Open seasonally ~April-Oct (April limited by flood risk). FCFS, no reservations; fee envelope/drop box at entrance. --Claude

name: Goose Island Campground
note: La Crosse County Parks campground 3 mi S of La Crosse on the Mississippi River - largest county campground in WI, ~300+ sites. Electric + water sites; no sewer; newer paved back-in/pull-thru sites in the south lanes handle large rigs (up to ~42 ft). Showers, laundry, dump station, camp store, swimming beach, 3 boat launches. Open mid-April-Oct. Reservable online or by phone. RV Life mis-tags it commercial; it is county-operated. (RV Life 4.5 star, $$) --Claude

name: Crystal Lake Campground
note: Village of Strum (Trempealeau County) municipal campground, 42 sites with water + 50-amp electric + cable, some full-hookup; dump station, showers. Open ~mid-May to October. Reservable by phone/email through the campground manager (no online portal, not on rec.gov). On Crystal Lake (dammed Buffalo River impoundment) with a boat landing. --Claude

name: Harbour Village Resort
note: Large private Door County resort campground/waterpark (~300 acres) in Carlsville. Public nightly RV sites bookable online (wooded/open pull-through + back-in, electric + water, dump station for sewer; no full hookups). Also runs UDI/condo and seasonal memberships, but transient public camping is confirmed across independent sources. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Inland off Hwy 42 with on-site swim/fishing ponds + waterpark, not on Green Bay. --Claude

name: Brown County Reforestation Camp Campground
note: Brown County Parks (E.J. Smith Reforestation Camp), Suamico. New 51-site campground opened 2022: 15 full-hookup (50-amp), 24 water + 30-amp electric, 8 rustic, plus walk-in tent/group/horse sites; gravel pads, dump station. 14-ft entrance height clearance (not a length limit). Open ~May to October. Reservable online via WebTrac only (no FCFS). --Claude

name: Upson Community Park
note: Community park at Upson (Iron County) on the Potato River near Upson Falls. 31 campsites, 10 with electric (20/30/50 amp incl. a pull-through), rest primitive; flush toilets, hot showers, pavilion, firewood, trout fishing. Electric $28/night ($168/wk); non-electric donation/$23. FCFS; drive-in. Firsthand review: 'amazingly well kept... beautiful campground.' Closes end of October. Phone not verified - omitted. (RV Life unrated). --Claude

name: Vernon County Fairgrounds Campground
note: Vernon County Fair Association campground at the county fairgrounds, Viroqua; 56 electric sites (50-amp available), two shower buildings, dump station. Open ~May-October except the week of the Vernon County Fair (a real season-long campground, not event-only). FCFS/contact office; flat grassy fairground sites fit large RVs. --Claude

name: Veterans Memorial Campground
note: La Crosse County park on Hwy 16, 1 mi W of West Salem along the La Crosse River. 100+ sites with electric and water hookups, sanitary dump station, restrooms/showers, canoe landing, La Crosse River State Trail access. Season ~Apr 15-Oct 15; primarily FCFS (county states reservations not accepted/needed), though limited online reservations exist via WebTrac; long stays by phone (608-789-8599). --Claude

name: Waterloo Recreation Area - Sugarloaf Lake Campground
note: Modern campground of Waterloo Recreation Area (Michigan DNR) on the west shore of Sugarloaf Lake, off Loveland Road (8200 Loveland Road, Chelsea, per the DNR directions); the Horsemen's equestrian campground is a separate campground a quarter-mile further along Loveland Road. Campers-only swim area and accessible boat launch; watercraft rentals for campers (734-355-0784); an accessible tiny house near the swim beach. Recycling available. --Claude

name: Fort Wilkins Historic State Park — West Loop
note: West campground of Fort Wilkins Historic State Park at the tip of the Keweenaw near Copper Harbor, on Lake Fanny Hooe west of the restored 1844 fort: two loops of shady sites with a playground between them; the park's boat ramp and accessible fishing pier are just west. Its own entrance road off US-41, separate from the East campground. --Claude

name: Fort Wilkins Historic State Park — East Loop
note: East campground of Fort Wilkins Historic State Park at the tip of the Keweenaw near Copper Harbor, on Lake Fanny Hooe east of the restored 1844 fort: several loops of sunny sites, two lake overlook decks and stairs down to the lake, a playground nearby. It has its own entrance road off US-41; the West campground is a separate entry west of the fort. Closed early 2026 for electrical and site upgrades; no closure notice since (rechecked 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-25). --Claude

name: Ionia Recreation Area - Modern Campground
note: Modern campground of Ionia Recreation Area (4,500 acres between Grand Rapids and Lansing), on a hilltop just east of Sessions Lake; two mini cabins sit in the campground. Reopened May 1 2026 after infrastructure upgrades. The park's separate equestrian and hike-in campgrounds are not part of this entry. --Claude

name: Newaygo State Park Campground
note: Rustic campground in two loops (Oak #1-48, Poplar #49-99) atop 20-ft embankments overlooking Hardy Dam Pond, a 6-mile flooding of the Muskegon River; large private sites with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers. Boat launch between the loops with a few mooring spots for registered campers, buoyed swim area in the Poplar loop, kayak rentals at the office early June to mid-September, 18-hole disc golf; borders the Manistee National Forest. Spongy moth larvae can surge in summer. --Claude

name: Leelanau State Park Campground
note: Rustic campground at the very tip of the Leelanau Peninsula beside the Grand Traverse Lighthouse (15310 N. Lighthouse Point Rd, Northport): rocky beach and big trees, about half the sites right on Lake Michigan and the rest tucked into the woods with lake views. Known for small sites: choose one the booking site rates for your rig. Three mini cabins in the campground; the park's Cathead Bay trails and sandy beach are on a separate unit 4 mi south. --Claude

name: Pinckney Recreation Area - Bruin Lake Modern Campground
note: Modern campground on Bruin Lake, one of a chain of seven lakes, at 21237 Kaiser Rd, Gregory; lower loop mostly paved, upper loop grass/dirt. Boat launch and a campers-only swim beach. Season ~Apr 15-Nov 1. --Claude

name: Twin Lakes State Park Campground
note: Single-loop modern campground of grass drive-in sites on the west shore of Lake Roland, about 26 miles from Houghton, near the designated swimming beach, boat launch and picnic area. Use the entrance at 32650 N. Hwy M-26, Toivola: some online resources give an address on Poyhonen Road, a logging road where turning a camper around is very difficult. ORVs may ride between the campground and the nearby trails (entering and exiting only). A base for the Porcupine Mountains and the Keweenaw. --Claude

name: Healy Lake State Forest Campground
note: Rustic state forest campground on Healy Lake, about 7.5 mi SW of Copemish (Manistee County), managed by Springdale Township. Sandy swimming beach and a boat ramp on the lake. Open about May 1 to Oct 31. A reviewer reports a 22-ft rig fit and large sites that could take a 30-ft trailer. --Claude

name: Houghton Lake State Forest Campground

season.note: Closed November to April (DNR amenity table).

season_source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Houghton Lake State Forest Campground: 'Seasonal closure dates: November to April'), read 2026-10-25
note: Semi-modern state forest campground on the north shore of Houghton Lake (Michigan's largest inland lake, 20,000+ acres; walleye, pike, bass, perch), 8 mi N of the town of Houghton Lake via West Houghton Lake Drive and Old US 27, Roscommon County; managed by North Higgins Lake State Park. Muskegon River 2 mi west, Higgins Lake 6 mi north. --Claude

name: Nichols Lake South Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Early May - Mid October'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/nichols-lake-south-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Early May - Mid October'; status 'Site Closed' on 2026-10-25), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on the south side of 160-acre Nichols Lake, 4.5 mi W of M-37 on 11 Mile Road (13.5 mi S of Baldwin). A wood ramp and stairs lead down to the lake; lakeside fishing path, paved boat launch, buoyed swim beach (no lifeguards) and accessible fishing pier. The North Country Trail passes the boat ramp; a separate day-use area is on the north side of the lake. --Claude

name: Bowman Bridge Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Early May - Mid October'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/bowman-bridge-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Early May - Mid October'; status 'Site Closed' on 2026-10-25), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground up the hill from Bowman Bridge Boat Landing on the Pere Marquette National Scenic River, ~5 mi west of Baldwin via W 52nd Street; concession-run (American Land & Leisure). Popular canoe and trout/steelhead fishing access; connector trail to the North Country Trail. --Claude

name: Pine Lake Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Early May - Labor Day'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/pine-lake-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Early May - Labor Day'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF rustic campground on the shore of Pine Lake (Manistee Co.); the east side of the lake is mostly private cabins, the federal west side swampy and long used by bald eagles. Shallow, gravel-bottomed swimming beach off the picnic area; boat access. Near the Big M cross-country ski / mountain-bike trails, the Pine National Scenic River and the Bear Track / North Country Trail area. --Claude

name: Old Grade Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Late April - Mid September'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/old-grade-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Late April - Mid September'; status 'Site Closed' on 2026-10-25), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on the Little Manistee River near Peacock, surrounded by National Forest land; a short interpretive trail with footbridges runs through hemlock and birch forest, and the nearby wetlands and fields are good for wildlife viewing. The river here is too shallow for canoeing but popular with trout and steelhead anglers. --Claude

name: Peterson Bridge Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Late April - Mid October'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/peterson-bridge-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Late April - Mid October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground, the only Forest Service campground on the Pine National Scenic River, on M-37 at the Pine River bridge 1.5 mi S of M-55 (21 mi N of Baldwin). Many RV sites are shaded and secluded; the riverbank tent sites can also be reached from the river. Canoe/boat launch across the river at Peterson Bridge North; a watercraft permit is required on the Pine from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. --Claude

name: Pines Point Campground

season.note: Forest Service: 'Early May - Mid October'.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/pines-point-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Early May - Mid October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on the banks of the White River near Hesperia, quiet and secluded under towering white pines, several sites overlooking the river. Walk-in canoe landing (a 30-60 minute float around the point) and a day-use area. Reached via 168th Ave / FR 5637. --Claude

name: Sand Lake Recreation Area Campground

season.note: 'Early May - Labor Day' (Forest Service).

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/sand-lake-recreation-area-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Early May - Labor Day'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground near Dublin and Wellston (Manistee Co.) on ~50-acre Sand Lake, mostly ringed by private land (the recreation area is the only public access): sandy swimming beach (the bottom turns mucky further out), boat ramp and picnic area. Wooded sites, some heavily shaded, on paved pads in two loops (sites 1-30 main loop, 30+ secondary loop); about 15 minutes from the Pine National Scenic River. This is the Sand Lake near Irons, not the one near Nottawa. --Claude

name: Seaton Creek Campground

season.note: Late April to early October (Forest Service).

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/seaton-creek-campground (Seasons of Use: 'Late April - Early October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Rustic Manistee NF campground adjoining Seaton Creek at the upper end of the Hodenpyl Dam backwater of the Big Manistee River, in mostly pine forest near a picnic area. Connector trail to the Manistee River Trail; the North Country Trail is across the suspension bridge over the Manistee. Kayakers can come up the very shallow Seaton Creek. Reached from M-37 by 26 Road, O'Rourke Drive and Forest Road 5993. --Claude

name: Bear Track Campground

season.note: Early May - Labor Day.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/bear-track-campground ('Seasons of Use: Early May - Labor Day'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on the Little Manistee River (a National Scenic Study River, known for steelhead and trout) in Lake County; about 16-20 sites with fire pits and picnic tables, plus walk-in riverside sites, and parking for 20 vehicles. Drive-in via FR 5202. A 1.5-mile trail connects the campground to the North Country National Scenic Trail. --Claude

name: Benton Lake Campground

season.note: Early May - Early September.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/benton-lake-campground ('Seasons of Use: Early May - Early September'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on 33-acre Benton Lake, entirely surrounded by National Forest land, in Newaygo County; boat launch (no-wake/electric-motor lake). Usually quiet, but very popular in hunting season. The North Country Trail crosses Pierce Drive about 2 miles east of the entrance road. --Claude

name: Hemlock Campground

season.note: Seasons of use: early May to Labor Day.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/hemlock-campground-and-boat-launch ('Seasons of Use Early May - Labor Day'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground and boat launch on the marshy west end of 1,600-acre Lake Mitchell near Cadillac (the lake is nearly surrounded by residences); good for wildlife viewing, but milfoil makes this end poor for swimming. Near the Cadillac West ORV and snowmobile trailhead. --Claude

name: Lake Michigan Recreation Area Campground

season.note: Early May to mid October (the FS page gives no exact dates).

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/huron-manistee/recreation/lake-michigan-recreation-area-campground ('Seasons of Use Early May - Mid October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Manistee NF campground on the Lake Michigan shore 15 mi south of Manistee (between Manistee and Ludington), along Porter Creek beside the Nordhouse Dunes Wilderness. Boardwalk/stairs to a sandy beach, overlook deck, amphitheater with peak-season programs, playground; the Arrowhead Trail loops between the campground and the beach and a Nordhouse Dunes trailhead is in the recreation area. 8 mi in from US-31 on Forest Trail Road (FS 5629). --Claude

name: Bobcat Lake Campground

season.note: Opens with full services the Friday before Memorial Day (subject to change). 2026: reduced services from October 15 (no water or garbage); usable until snow limits access or January 1, whichever comes first.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/bobcat-lake-campground ('The campground is scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day'; 'Reduced services beginning October 15, 2026, no water or garbage services will be provided. Visitors can use the facility until snow conditions reduce access or January 1st, whichever is sooner'), read 2026-10-25
note: Ottawa NF campground on Bobcat Lake, ~3 mi SE of Marenisco on FR 8500 off M-64, Bessemer RD; run by concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Swimming beach and day-use area half a mile east. --Claude

name: Bob Lake Campground

season.note: 'The campground is scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day. This date is subject to change.' No closing date posted.

note: Ottawa NF campground on 133-acre Bob Lake, ~18 mi SE of Ontonagon, Ontonagon RD; run by concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. Many sites near the lake; adjacent day-use picnic area, boat landing and the 1.2-mile Beaver Lodge Interpretive Trail. Shallow lake (3-17 ft) with walleye, smallmouth bass and perch. Reached via FH 16, FR 1640 (Pori Road), FR 1470 and FR 1478. --Claude

name: Henry Lake Campground

season.note: Seasons of use May 15 - October 15; opens with full services the Friday before Memorial Day (subject to change). 2026: reduced services from October 15 (no water or garbage); usable until snow limits access or January 1, whichever comes first.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/henry-lake-campground ('Seasons of Use May 15 – October 15'; 'The campground is scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day'; 'Reduced services beginning October 15, 2026, no water or garbage services will be provided. Visitors can use the facility until snow conditions reduce access or January 1st, whichever is sooner.'), read 2026-10-25
note: Ottawa NF campground beside Henry Lake (bass, bluegill), Bessemer Ranger District, 9 mi SW of Marenisco via FR 8100. A single loop of drive-in sites screened by natural vegetation; free concrete boat ramp with trailer parking, and a trail from the landing to an accessible fishing pier. Run by the concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. --Claude

name: Imp Lake Campground

season.note: Seasons of use May 15 - October 15; opens with full services the Friday before Memorial Day (subject to change). 2026: Loop 1's gate closes October 15; Loop 2 has reduced services from October 15 (no water or garbage) and is usable until snow limits access or January 1, whichever comes first.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/ottawa/recreation/imp-lake-campground ('Seasons of Use May 15 – October 15'; 'The campground is scheduled to open with full services the Friday before Memorial Day'; 'Loop 1 - Gate will close on October 15, 2026. Loop 2 - Reduced services begin October 15, 2026; no water or garbage services will be provided. Visitors can use the facility until snow conditions reduce access or January 1, whichever is sooner.'), read 2026-10-25
note: Ottawa NF campground on 111-acre, no-wake Imp Lake (trout, panfish), 6 mi SE of Watersmeet via US 2 and FR 3978, Watersmeet Ranger District. Two loops of screened drive-in sites: lakeside sites look onto a small island with nesting loons, off-lake sites sit beside towering hemlocks. Free concrete boat ramp and picnic area beside the campground, and the 1-mile wheelchair-accessible Imp Lake Interpretive Trail across the road. Run by the concessionaire Camp Host, LLC. --Claude

name: En Gedi Resort & Canoe Livery

season.note: 'Open Memorial Day Weekend Through Labor Day Weekend'.

note: Family campground on the St. Joseph River near Leonidas with an on-site canoe/kayak livery, a River Trail to the fishing and swimming area, and rental cottages; a no-alcohol, no-marijuana Christian-oriented family resort. One RV or up to two tents per site; no sleeping in cars, vans or trucks. --Claude

name: Twin Pines Campground & Canoe Livery
note: Family-owned since the early 1970s on nearly 50 wooded acres along the Kalamazoo River near Hanover, with a canoe/kayak livery. Directory listings (not the operator) describe electric+water and primitive sites, a May - mid-October season and nightly rates around $35-40. --Claude

name: Cadillac Woods Campground
note: Private wooded campground on M-115 in Tustin, SE of Cadillac; RV and rustic tent sites plus rental cabins, clubhouse, pool, mini-golf. Open May-Oct; nightly stays, and a discounted monthly rate by phone. --Claude

name: Kestelwoods Campground
note: Family-owned campground between Cadillac and Manistee in the Manistee NF, near the Pine, Manistee and Pere Marquette rivers, with ORV trails reachable straight from the park; a 30-ft rental trailer is set up on a site. --Claude

name: Houghton Lake Travel Park Campground

season.note: Camping April through October; in 2026 the campground closes for the season on Monday, October 19, with site water off from October 5.

season_source: https://www.houghtonlaketravelparkcampground.com/rates/ ('Camping Rates April thru October') + home page ('The entire campground will close for the season on Monday, October 19', 'turn water off to individual campsites on Monday, October 5'), read 2026-10-22
note: Private family campground near Houghton Lake, Michigan's largest inland lake, with cabins and a primitive tent area beside the camper sites; heated pool, coffee shop, game room. A Christian, family-oriented park that does not tolerate rowdy behavior, drunkenness or loud music. --Claude

name: Northern Exposure Campground
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: Large campground on 300 wooded acres with 2.5 miles of frontage on Hodenpyle Pond, a Manistee River impoundment near Mesick, with waterfront and inland sites on paved roads.  Open April to October. --Claude

name: Betsie River Campsite

season.note: Operator: 'We open when the ground thaws and we can turn the water on ... April-ish to October-ish'.

season_source: https://www.betsieriver.com/faq ('When do you open/close for the season? ... April-ish to October-ish....ish'), read 2026-10-22
note: Small family-owned campground at 1923 River Road near Frankfort/Elberta, inside the Betsie River State Game Refuge about 400 swampy feet from the river (no river access from camp). Self-described as 'not a big concrete pad RV park' but takes campers and travel trailers; quiet, family-oriented, room for a boat on most sites. Betsie Valley Trail at hand; beaches about 3 miles. --Claude

name: Michihistrigan Campground
note: Byce's Michihistrigan Campground, Bar and Cabins: a 37-acre wooded campground attached to a bar & grill in Gould City, on snowmobile trail #2; tent and rustic camping, six cabins, stone pavilion, disc golf. Directory listings (not the operator) describe restrooms, showers, laundry and a store, mini golf, archery and trout ponds, and a season of about May 1-Dec 1. Nightly transient plus some seasonal. --Claude

name: Kewadin Casino RV Park (Sault Ste. Marie)
note: Sault Ste. Marie Tribe of Chippewa Indians' casino RV park at the casino's southwest entrance: a dedicated hookup park sold by the night (and by the 30 days), not a parking-lot allowance; RV guests use the hotel's showers, indoor pool and fitness room. --Claude

name: JoeIda Campground

season.note: Open May-October (2024 season May 23 - October 16).

season_source: https://joeidacampground.com/contact-us ('Open May23 Closing October 16 2024', 'Open May-October'), read 2026-10-22
note: Small secluded rustic campground (opened 2017) on Russ Lake Rd ~1 mi off H-58, between Munising and Grand Marais in the Pictured Rocks area, a mile south of Kingston Lake. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table; also three off-grid cabins. Dry camping; generators 10 am-6 pm only; ATVs allowed on the campground road. Private land: no national lakeshore pass needed. --Claude

name: Cade Lake County Park & Campground

season.note: First Friday of May through the Sunday before Columbus Day.

season_source: https://pub-003a708fde47491d8119c0c7bc46e250.r2.dev/2026/05/2796_638530168317670000.pdf ('Camping Season: The first Friday of May through the Sunday prior to Columbus Day in October'), read 2026-10-22
note: St. Joseph County Parks campground on 32-acre Cade Lake (RV Life mis-tags it commercial; it is county-operated). About 43 full-hookup sites and 9 rustic sites plus cabins; nightly sites alongside seasonal leases. Bookable from Feb 1. GPS may lead big rigs onto narrow back roads; the county says to approach via US 12. --Claude

name: Hillsdale County Fairgrounds Campground

season.note: April to October, excluding fair week (subject to change). During fair week camping is limited to vendors, open-class and 4-H exhibitors.

season_source: https://www.hillsdalecountyfair.org/camping ('Excluding fair week, the park is open from April to October (subject to change)') + https://www.hillsdalecountyfair.org/faq ('Camping space during fair week is limited to vendors, open class and 4-H exhibitors'), read 2026-10-22
note: Shaded campground at the Hillsdale County Fairgrounds, open for general overnight camping through the season except fair week; licensed campground groups welcome. --Claude

name: Branch County Fairgrounds Campground

season.note: 'Excluding fair week, the park is open from May to October (subject to change).' Fair week is in August (August 8-14 in 2027).

note: Branch County fairgrounds in Coldwater, a licensed campground open to campers outside fair week; flat open terrain. Fires in above-ground pits only. --Claude

name: Walnut Grove Campground (Lower Huron Metropark)

season.note: Sites can be reserved early May through mid-October.

season_source: https://www.metroparks.com/lower-huron-metropark/ ('Thirty campsites are located near the Huron River and can be reserved early May through mid-October'), read 2026-10-22
note: Huron-Clinton Metroparks (regional authority) campground in Lower Huron Metropark, on the Huron River near Belleville; modern restrooms, near the Turtle Cove aquatic center and the hike-bike trail. Reviewers fit 40-ft and 31-ft rigs fine. Renovated and reopened 2023. --Claude

name: Eaton County Fairgrounds

season.note: Open to the public mid-April to mid-October (no exact dates posted).

season_source: https://eatoncountyfair.com/pageserver/camping ('Campground open to public Mid-April to Mid-October'; 'Our campground is OPEN!'), read 2026-10-22
note: Transient campground at the Eaton County Fairgrounds in Charlotte, open to the public all season (closed during the July fair and certain large events) - a real all-season campground, not fair-week-only. Pick an open site and the camp hosts collect the fee. Run by the Eaton County Agricultural Society (the member fair board, not county government), so ownership recorded as private. --Claude

name: St. Clair Boat Harbor Campground
note: City-owned Charles F. Moore Memorial municipal boat harbor at 902 S. Second St., on the St. Clair River at the mouth of the Pine River, an easy walk from downtown restaurants and shopping, with fire pits and a free shuttle within the city. Drive-in; small flat harbor sites fit a 23-ft RV. The harbor is staffed April 1 - October 15. Online booking at midnrreservations.com covers the harbor's boat slips only, not the campsites; call the harbor office (2026-10-22). --Claude

name: Shiawassee County Fairgrounds Campground
note: Operated by the Shiawassee County Agricultural Society (private nonprofit, not county government) at 2900 Hibbard Rd, Corunna, between Flint and Lansing. General overnight RV camping outside fair week, April-October 1; fair-week camping is by exhibitor lottery only. Primitive sites besides the electric ones; specializes in group camping/camper rallies and hosts show campers (the camping rules cover barns and horse trailers). Site count not published. --Claude

name: Wabasis Lake Campground

season.note: Last weekend in April through the last weekend in October.

season_source: https://www.kentcountymi.gov/1722/Wabasis-Lake-Campground ('Season Last weekend in April through the last weekend in October'), read 2026-10-22
note: Kent County Parks campground in 104-acre Wabasis Lake Park, which has over a mile of shoreline on 400-acre Wabasis Lake; large sand beach and boat ramp; cabins and a lakefront cottage also rent. --Claude

name: Pioneer County Park

season.note: First Friday in May through the last Sunday in September (2026: May 1 - Sept 27).

season_source: https://muskegoncountyparks.org/pioneer-park/ ('The campground is open from the first Friday in May through the last Sunday in September'), read 2026-10-22
note: Muskegon County park on the Lake Michigan shore at 1563 N. Scenic Dr., North Muskegon, with 2,000 ft of beach reached by stairs, overlook decks, courts and a playground; sites sit in forested sand dunes. --Claude

name: Croton Township Campground

season.note: The site posts no campground season; it says 'Limited winter camping available'. Dock season May 1 - October 31, weather permitting.

season_source: https://www.crotontownshipcampground.com/campsites-rates ('Limited winter camping available'; 'Dock season is May 1 - October 31, weather permitting'), read 2026-10-25
note: Township campground on Croton Dam Pond, the 1,380-acre Muskegon River impoundment above Croton Dam, at 7683 S Croton Hardy Dr, Newaygo: waterfront and wooded lots, two boat launches, dock rentals, a small sandy beach. Walking distance to restaurants, stores and gas. --Claude

name: Meinert County Park - Pines Campground

season.note: Campsite fee season: first Friday in May to last Sunday in September.

season_source: https://muskegoncountyparks.org/meinert-park/ ('Campsite Fee: First Friday in May – Last Sunday in September'), read 2026-10-22
note: Muskegon County park near Montague (8390 Meinert Park Rd) in 182 acres of forested Lake Michigan dunes along Little Flower Creek; open and shaded sites, several paved, about 2,000 ft from the Lake Michigan beach. A three-bedroom rental cottage. --Claude

name: Haymarsh Lake Campground (Haymarsh State Game Area)
note: Rustic Mecosta County Parks campground on Haymarsh Lake (375 acres, a 1949 flooding that joined six small lakes) within the DNR's 6,737-acre Haymarsh Lake State Game Area, ~7 mi E of Paris; public hunting land access. Open ~May-Dec 1. Max RV length not published -- sites described as spacious, but firsthand big-rig confirmation lacking. --Claude

name: Mason County Campground
note: Mason County (county government) campground, 5906 W Chauvez Rd, Ludington, under tall hardwoods; a nature path leads to the picnic area and disc golf course, and Lake Michigan is under 5 minutes away. Inland/wooded, no water body. Open roughly Memorial Day-Labor Day. Distinct facility from the Mason County Fairgrounds campground ~4 mi away. --Claude

name: City of Au Gres Riverfront Campground

season.note: Second weekend of April through the second weekend of October.

season_source: https://augresriverfrontcampground.com/reservation-request/ ('Campsites will be available for reservations after January 2nd for the current year of the 2nd weekend of April though the 2nd weekend of October'), read 2026-10-22; the derived 04-15 / 10-15 fall outside those weekends and are cleared
note: City of Au Gres municipal campground, 522 Park St, on the Au Gres River near Saginaw Bay; city-run since the 1960s. Lighted riverfront walkway with a footbridge into town, kayak rentals at the office, boat launch. Distinct from Arenac County's separate Point Au Gres Park. --Claude

name: Thurston Park Campground

season.note: The first Friday in May to the first Sunday in October.

season_source: https://centrallakemi.org/thurston-park/ ('Our camping season spans from the first Friday in May to the first Sunday in October') + the Guide ('The park opens the first Friday in May and closes the first Sunday in October'), read 2026-10-25
note: Village of Central Lake park at the northwest end of Intermediate Lake (Antrim County Chain of Lakes), 7854 Bradford St. Boat launch, public docks, gazebo, playground, fish-cleaning station; easy walk to downtown. --Claude

name: Magnus Park
note: City of Petoskey municipal campground on Little Traverse Bay at the end of West Lake St (901 W Lake St), with 1,000 ft of shoreline: about 36 full-hookup and 39 water/electric sites plus cabins, and a beach; walkable to Bayfront Park, the Little Traverse Wheelway and downtown. Open ~May 2-Oct 11. --Claude

name: O.B. Fuller Park and Campground
note: Delta County park on 82 acres ~15 mi south of Escanaba on M-35, in northern forest where the Bark River meets Lake Michigan; sandy beach, small boat launch, two playgrounds; rustic cabins and tent sites in a hemlock stand. Reservations open Dec 1; season opens in May. --Claude

name: Lake Antoine Park
note: Dickinson County park on Lake Antoine with a beach, boat launch and swimming. Operates Memorial Day through Labor Day. --Claude

name: Pentoga Park
note: Iron County park on Chicagon Lake (1630 County Rd 424, Crystal Falls). Beach (no lifeguard) with a changing house, waterfront cook stoves, playground; historic Chippewa (Ojibwa) burial grounds preserved on site. Opens the Friday before Memorial Day through September. --Claude

name: Runkle Lake Park Campground
note: City of Crystal Falls park on Runkle Lake, run by a private concessionaire (Runkle Lake Camping; still city-owned), walking distance from downtown. ~33 sites (1-17 full hookup, 18-33 water/electric) plus primitive tent sites. Sandy beach, boat launch, fishing pier, lakeside playground; next to the city sports complex, with Iron Belle Trail access, and ATVs/ORVs may use Iron County roads. --Claude

name: Newberg Park Campground (Sagola Township)
note: Sagola Township park on Sawyer Lake near Channing (N12886 Sawyer Lake Rd, 25 acres); beach with good swimming, boat launch, pavilion, playground. Campground hosts on site May 11 - Oct 1 (2026 schedule); by reservation through the host. --Claude

name: Luce County Park & Campground

season.note: Open Memorial Day through October, weather permitting (the county gives no closing date).

season_source: https://www.lucecountymi.com/parks-recreation ('OPEN: Memorial Day through October ?- Weather Permitting.'), read 2026-10-22
note: Luce County Parks & Rec park on North Manistique Lake at 3266 CR-478, McMillan; swimming beach, boat launch. Mix of first-come sites ($19) and online-reservable sites ($34); the county's own page posts no camping rate. Accepts big rigs. --Claude

name: Lake Gogebic County Park

season.note: Camping season mid-May to late September (2027: to September 26); seasonal sites may be occupied mid-May to the end of September.

season_source: https://www.gogebicforestryandparks.com/lakegogebic ('Mid-May-September 26, 2027 (During camping season)'; 'seasonal sites which can be occupied from mid-May to the end of September'), read 2026-10-22
note: On the SW shore of Lake Gogebic (N8598 Hwy M-64, Marenisco), run by Gogebic County Forestry & Parks; boat launch, pier, swimming area, pavilion, playground, camper waste removal service. Many sites are seasonal (including lakeside ones); the rest are nightly or monthly. Sites fit RVs to ~50 ft. (Distinct from Lake Gogebic STATE PARK ~3 mi away.) --Claude

name: Stannard Township Park
note: Township-run RV park on US-45 in Bruce Crossing (14190 US-45), operated by Stannard Township (local government; RV Life mislabels as commercial). Gravel pads beside a strip of grass in an open field by the road (road noise); utilities are shared between pairs of sites, so neighbours park facing opposite ways; honor-system payment. Google reviewers report $15 a night (2025) and some RVs staying long-term. Open ~May 15-Oct 31. --Claude

name: L'Anse Township Park & Campground

season.note: Camping season mid May - mid October; the park's trails are open year-round.

note: L'Anse Township park 2 mi north of L'Anse (15829 Skanee Road), on a sloping hillside above Keweenaw Bay (Lake Superior), the site of the first trading post and original townsite of L'Anse. Pavilion, playground, Lake Superior beach, dock and gazebo. ~$35/night RV. --Claude

name: Rocky Neck State Park
note: CT DEEP state park on Long Island Sound. 160 wooded/grassy sites in 5 loops (Heron, Egret, Crane, Osprey, Seagull), plus 3 cabins. No RV hookups; dump station and water spigots on site. Sites fit rigs up to 35 ft (some tent-only). Reservable via Reserve America; 2026 season ~May into late Sept. --Claude

name: Salt Rock State Campground
note: CT DEEP state campground (former private campground, now state-run). 71 tent/RV sites incl. ~14 full hookups, electric and electric+water sites; sites 1-7 upgraded to 50-amp. Flush toilets, showers, dump station. Max RV/trailer ~35 ft (some sites much smaller). Season ~early May-mid Oct. Reservable via Reserve America. --Claude

name: Lake Waramaug State Park
note: CT state park on Lake Waramaug. 76 sites (plus rustic cabins) in wooded and open settings. No hookups (rustic). Restrooms, showers, drinking water, dump station. Max RV/trailer 35 ft. No pets, no alcohol. Season Memorial Day weekend-Columbus Day. Reservable via Reserve America. --Claude

name: Housatonic Meadows State Park
note: CT state park on the Housatonic River near Cornwall Bridge. ~95 sites (57 reservable) under tall pines. No hookups; drinking water, flush toilets, showers, dump station; 5 pull-through sites. Max RV/trailer 35 ft. No pets, no alcohol. Season ~May 22-Sep 7. Reservable via Reserve America. --Claude

name: Mashamoquet Brook State Park — Wolf Den Campground
note: Wolf Den loop at Mashamoquet Brook SP. 35 mostly-open sites (1-35) with paved level pads, flush toilets, showers, drinking water (through Labor Day); water/electric hookup at site 20 only, otherwise no hookups; dump station (reported closed until further notice). Wide gravel/paved roads fit moderately sized RVs/larger trailers. Pets prohibited. Season ~May 22-Sep 7. Reservable via Reserve America (48-hr advance, no walk-ins). --Claude

name: Mashamoquet Brook State Park — Brook Campground
note: Brook loop at Mashamoquet Brook SP -- the smaller, more wooded/private of the park's two campgrounds. 18 wooded sites, short walk to Mashamoquet Brook. Primitive: portable toilets, no running water/showers. Gravel roads fit moderately sized RVs/larger trailers (RV/tent). Pets prohibited. Season ~May 1-Oct 12. Reservable via Reserve America. --Claude

name: American Legion State Forest — Austin F. Hawes Memorial Campground
note: CT state forest campground (Austin F. Hawes Memorial) on the West Branch Farmington River near Pleasant Valley. 30 sites (plus rustic cabins) in pine woods. Primitive -- no hookups; bathrooms, showers, dump station. Season ~mid-Apr-Columbus Day. Reservable via Reserve America. --Claude

name: Circle C Campground
note: Private family campground at 21 Bailey Pond Rd, Voluntown, near Bailey Pond; 118 sites incl. 10 pull-throughs, 114 W/E. Open mid-Apr to mid-Oct. Takes reservations (nightly/weekly/monthly); laundry, showers, dump station, propane. --Claude

name: Highland Campground
note: Private campground at 42 Toleration Rd, Scotland; 116 W/E (20/30A) sites, accommodates rigs to 60 ft. Open May-Oct. Heavily seasonal ($2,550/season) but accepts nightly reservations (call/email; age 21+). Showers, laundry, dog park, weekend activities. --Claude

name: Wilgus State Park
note: VT FPR state park on the Connecticut River (Weathersfield/Ascutney). 26 reservable units: 15 tent/RV sites + 6 lean-tos + group lean-to area + 4 electric cabins. Max RV/trailer length 35 ft (pull-through at T01); a 23-ft rig fits. No hookups at sites; dump station + potable fill at entrance. Season ~early May-mid Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Mount Ascutney State Park
note: VT FPR state park at the base of Mt. Ascutney (campground on a normal paved road; the steep auto road is the separate summit toll road). Two loops, ~49 units: tent/RV + tent-only + 10 lean-tos + cabins. Most drive-in sites cap at 20 ft - only a few fit a 23-ft rig (e.g. T05=34 ft, T19=28 ft), so reserve a length-appropriate site. No hookups; dump station on site. Season ~mid May-mid Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Quechee State Park
note: VT FPR state park near Quechee Gorge (Hartford). ~45 tent/RV sites + 7 lean-tos + 6 cabins in wooded back-in loops; RV length varies ~20-35 ft, a 23-ft rig fits. No hookups; dump station on site, flush toilets, hot showers. Campground on plateau ~165 ft above the Ottauquechee River in the gorge. Season ~late May-mid Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Bomoseen State Park
note: VT FPR state park on the west shore of Lake Bomoseen (Castleton). Loop A, 64 reservable units: 42 tent/RV + 12 tent-only + 10 lean-tos; RV length to 34-35 ft, a 23-ft rig fits easily. No hookups; dump station, flush toilets, hot showers. Season ~late May-early Sep, reservable online. --Claude

name: Gifford Woods State Park
note: VT FPR state park near Killington off VT Route 100. 45 reservable units across Upper/Lower loops: 16 tent/RV + 6 tent-only + 19 lean-tos + 4 electric cabins; FPR notes several tent/RV sites won't fit an RV, but larger sites reach 35 ft (T13) so a 23-ft rig fits - reserve a longer site. No hookups; dump station, coin hot showers. Season ~late May-mid Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Half Moon Pond State Park
note: VT FPR state park on Half Moon Pond (Hubbardton, near Bomoseen). 69 reservable units: 40 tent/RV + 12 tent-only + 11 lean-tos + 5 cabins + 1 cottage; no park-wide length cap, tent/RV sites to 35 ft, a 23-ft rig fits comfortably. No hookups at tent/RV sites; dump station on site. Season ~late May-mid Oct, reservable online (FCFS for unbooked sites). --Claude

name: Silver Lake State Park
note: VT state park on Silver Lake (Barnard), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation. 39 tent/RV sites + 7 lean-tos. Drive-in (park at your site); max trailer 30 ft / RV 34 ft, no driving restrictions. No hookups; sanitary dump station, token hot showers, sandy beach with boat rentals. Season ~late May-early Sep. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

name: Branbury State Park
note: VT state park on Lake Dunmore (Brandon/Salisbury), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation. ~36 tent/RV sites + 7 lean-tos, split by Rte 53: open grassy beach-side loop (level, larger-rig friendly) and a wooded hillside loop (narrow/twisty/dead-ends - scout before towing). Max RV/trailer length ~20-35 ft by site. No hookups; sanitary dump station, 1,000-ft sandy beach, boat rentals. Season ~mid-May-Columbus Day. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

name: Allis State Park
note: VT state park on Bear Hill summit (Brookfield), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation. ~18 tent/RV sites + 8 lean-tos (group lean-to + pavilion too). Per-site max RV/trailer 20-35 ft; 23-ft rig fits (firsthand 28-ft trailer at site 1). No hookups; dump station, flush toilets, coin hot showers, lookout tower. Season ~late May-early Sep. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

name: DAR State Park
note: VT state park (Daughters of the American Revolution) on Lake Champlain (Addison), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation. ~42-47 tent/RV sites + 24 lean-tos (+ pavilion). Per-site max RV/trailer 20-35 ft (some 35-ft pull-throughs). No hookups; dump station, flush toilets, coin hot showers, boat launch. Picnic area on a bluff above the lake; rocky/shale beach via stairs. Season ~late May-early Sep. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

name: Button Bay State Park
note: VT state park on a bluff over Lake Champlain (Ferrisburgh), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation. ~49 tent/RV sites + 4 tent-only + 13 lean-tos + 4 cabins. Max RV/trailer length 31 ft. No hookups; sanitary dump station, water available, swimming via a meadow trail down to the beach. Season ~late May-mid-Oct. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica), 2-night min >7 days out. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights when booked more than 7 days ahead, single nights inside 7 days (vtstateparks.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Ricker Pond State Park
note: VT state park in Groton State Forest on 95-acre Ricker Pond (Groton), run by VT Dept. of Forests, Parks & Recreation (state). ~12 tent/RV (Sec. C tent & trailer) + 14 tent-only + 23 lean-tos (Sec. A on the pond) + cabins/cottages. Max RV/trailer ~20-28 ft by site; only a few fit ~25 ft - verify site length for a 23-ft rig. No hookups; water spigots, dump station, coin showers. Bears active - secure food. Season ~late May-Columbus Day. Reservable online (ReserveAmerica) or FCFS for open sites. --Claude

name: Big Deer State Park
note: VT State Park campground in Groton State Forest, off Boulder Beach Rd (well-graded dirt, normal-vehicle passable); check-in at neighboring Stillwater SP. 26 sites: 21 tent/RV + 5 lean-to. Per-site max equipment length 20-35 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits. NO hookups (dump station only). Season ~late May to early Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Brighton State Park
note: VT State Park on Spectacle Pond, off State Park Rd (standard graded access). ~82 sites in three pond-side loops: ~47 tent/RV + 7 tent-only + 23 lean-to + 5 cabins (cabins electric). Largest site 30 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits. NO hookups at sites (dump station only). Season ~late May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Lake Carmi State Park
note: Large VT State Park on Lake Carmi via Marsh Farm Rd (paved campground roads). 175 sites: 132 tent/RV + 6 tent-only + 35 lean-to + 2 cabins (electric), in two lakefront loops (Area A and B). Per-site max length 15-35 ft, so 23-ft rig fits (some interior sites cap low - site selection matters). NO hookups at sites (dump station, flush toilets, hot showers). Season mid-May to mid-Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Greendale Campground
note: Green Mountain National Forest (USFS), Weston. Small remote campground along Greendale Brook, ~9-11 back-in sites. First-come-first-served only (not on recreation.gov); ~$10/night. No hookups, no drinking water, vault toilet. Spurs are short -- Forest Service guidance says best for RVs under ~24 ft, so a 23-ft rig is near the upper limit; some sites take small campers/trailers/camper vans. Open seasonally (Memorial Day-Labor Day). --Claude

name: Prouty Beach & Campground
note: City of Newport (Newport Parks & Recreation) municipal campground on Lake Memphremagog. Over 75 campsites, RV (up to ~40 ft) and tent including primitive tent sites; full hookups available (50-amp water/electric/sewer per listings). Open late Apr through mid-Oct. Reservable online and by phone. --Claude

name: Bald Mountain Campground
note: Private family campground (est. 1968) on 160+ acres along the West River at 1760 State Forest Rd, Townshend. ~190 open and wooded sites, 62 pull-through; many sites on the West River or the beaver pond. Mix of nightly and seasonal sites plus a separate tent area and group camping. Water & electric or water-only; dump station, laundry, showers. Open May through Columbus Day. Reserve by phone or email. Source: operator reservations page. --Claude

name: Groton Forest Road Campground
note: Private commercial campground at 2654 VT-232, Marshfield, just N of Groton State Forest. 32 sites (RV + tent), 9 pull-throughs, max RV 40 ft; 15/30-amp electric + water, dump station, showers, laundry, store. Open May-Oct. Mixed transient + seasonal with real nightly availability; reservable by phone. Its old website no longer resolves. Ownership changed ~2022. --Claude

name: Hazen's Notch Campground
note: Privately owned, family-operated 30+ years at 185 Green Hill Rd, Lowell (NOT the hike-in Hazen's Notch ski center). 50 sites: 30 RV (water, 30/50-amp electric, sewer; some full-hookup) + 20 tent/trailer. Dump station, hot showers, firewood. Drive-in (gravel/dirt road off Rte 58, passable); park-next-to-site. Open ~May-Oct. Transient nightly (~$30-50) plus weekly/monthly/seasonal. Reserve by phone; no online booking. Max RV length not published. --Claude

name: Barrewood Campground
note: Small private campground (Barrewood Campground Inc.) at 3102 VT-100, Westfield. 38 sites: ~6 full hookup, ~32 electric/water (20/30-amp), 6 pull-throughs, 5 tent-only; accepts big rigs (~55-60 ft). Camp store, showers, laundry, pool, playground. Open seasonally ~May 1 - Oct 15. Transient nightly ($44 W/E, $48 W/E/S); Passport America honored. Reservable by phone (802-744-6340 alt), not online. --Claude

name: Monadnock State Park (Gilson Pond Campground)
note: Gilson Pond camping area at Monadnock SP: 41 sites total (16 tent-only, 12 platform, 5 RV/trailer up to 30 ft, 3 standard up to 25 ft, plus 5 remote hike-to). A 23-ft RV fits the RV/Trailer sites. No hookups per official reservation page. Flush toilets, showers, drinking water, small camp store. Season ~May 1-Oct 11. Reservable online/by phone via NH State Parks (ReserveAmerica). --Claude  Correction 2026-10-12: the booking site now lists 30-amp electric (no water or sewer) on the five RV/Trailer sites, which cost $45 a night against $35 for the others. --Claude

name: Greenfield State Park
note: Largest campground in the NH State Park system on Otter Lake: ~252 back-in gravel sites ranging ~20-38 ft, one camping unit per site. NO hookups. Drinking water, flush toilets, showers, camp store, beaches. ~175 sites reservable, remainder FCFS. Season ~mid-May to Columbus Day. Reservable online/by phone via NH State Parks. --Claude

name: Pawtuckaway State Park
note: ~190+ sites on Pawtuckaway Lake across Big Island, Horse Island, and Neals Cove loops (~55 tent-only; 100+ take pop-ups/trailers/motorhomes). Most sites fit rigs up to 24 ft; select sites up to 38 ft, so a 23-ft RV fits. NO hookups. Showers, drinking water, beach. Season ~May-Oct. Reservable online/by phone via NH State Parks; some FCFS. Note: Neals Cove access road is reportedly rough. --Claude

name: Bear Brook State Park
note: Beaver Pond campground at Bear Brook SP: ~101 wooded primitive sites, ~36 RV-friendly (RV spaces limited to 38 ft due to narrow roads/smaller sites). NO water/electric hookups (one site has 30-amp). Showers, vault toilets, dump station, camp store, swim beach, canoe rentals. Reservable via NH State Parks (ReserveAmerica); some FCFS. Season ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Pillsbury State Park
note: Primitive 41-site campground at Pillsbury SP around Butterfield/May Pond: 14 standard drive-in sites, 6 tent-only, 4 small-popup/tent sites, 11 remote/canoe/walk-in sites. Standard sites listed up to 38 ft max, so a 23-ft rig fits the larger standard sites (some are small). NO electricity/hookups; vault toilets, drinking water; cash only on-site. Reservable via NH State Parks (ReserveAmerica). Season ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: White Lake State Park
note: NH state park on White Lake (Tamworth/W. Ossipee). ~200 wooded sites across two camping areas; tents, trailers and RVs (12 tent-only sites). No hookups; dump station and communal water spigots; flush toilets, coin-op showers. Max RV ~38 ft but many sites smaller-check length when booking. Open Memorial Day weekend to ~mid-Oct; reservable via ReserveAmerica with some FCFS sites held. --Claude

name: Moose Brook State Park
note: NH state park campground in Gorham (30 Jimtown Rd), ~56-59 wooded sites on two sides of a road. Largest sites ~30 ft-OK for a 23-ft rig, not for big rigs. No hookups, no dump station; potable water spigots, full restrooms, showers. Spring-fed swimming pond on Moose Brook. Reservable Memorial Day-Columbus Day via ReserveAmerica, FCFS off-season; open ~May-late Oct. --Claude

name: Jericho Mountain State Park
note: NH state park campground near Berlin (298 Jericho Lake Rd) by Jericho Lake. 9 RV sites (two pull-through to 40 ft, rest back-in 24-36 ft) plus 4 tent sites, 2 Adirondack shelters and 5 cabins (RV sites are the basis for inclusion). No hookups; flush toilets, showers, laundry. Day-use beach, boat launch and 75+ mi ATV trail network. Reservable up to 11 mo via ReserveAmerica; open through late Oct. --Claude

name: Umbagog Lake State Park
note: 32-site drive-in base campground at the south end of Umbagog Lake (Cambridge/Errol, NH, off Rt 26). Mix of standard, pop-up/tent, tent-only sites and 2 lean-tos; electric (15-30A) and water hookups at base, dump station, camp store, flush/pit toilets and coin showers, canoe/kayak rentals. Back-in sites; max equipment length varies 10-24 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits only the larger sites. Open Memorial Day weekend through Columbus Day weekend (2026: May 22-Oct 11). Reservable via ReserveAmerica; FCFS walk-ins also welcome. A separate 35 boat/paddle-in remote sites are NOT included here. Operator: NH Division of Parks & Recreation. --Claude

name: Mollidgewock State Park
note: Primitive ~42-44 site campground along the Androscoggin River in the Thirteen Mile Woods Scenic Area, ~3 mi south of Errol. Mostly tent-only and pop-up/tent plus 2 lean-tos and remote canoe-to sites; 2 'standard' drive-in sites accommodate small trailers/RVs (site #029 is a 25 ft pull-through), so a 23-ft rig fits the standard sites only. NO hookups; pit toilets, potable water, fire rings; wood/ice and canoe/kayak rentals on site. Open Memorial Day weekend through Columbus Day weekend (2026: May 22-Oct 11). Reservable via ReserveAmerica; self-registration for walk-ins. Operator: NH Division of Parks & Recreation. RV Life: unrated (0*) / $ --Claude

name: Coleman State Park
note: NH State Parks campground in Stewartstown on Little Diamond Pond, Great North Woods. ~36 reservable units total (standard, pop-up/tent, tent-only, lean-to, cabins, group); drive-in standard/pop-up sites fit self-contained RVs, up to 40 ft on select pull-through sites. NO hookups; dump station, flush toilets, coin showers. All sites ATV-trail accessible. Season ~May 15-Oct 11. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica (some FCFS sites at campground). Operated by NH Division of Parks & Recreation. Limited/no cell service. --Claude

name: Lake Francis State Park
note: NH State Parks campground in Pittsburg on 2,000-acre Lake Francis, Great North Woods. 45 drive-in sites incl. 9 with water/electric (20-amp) hookups (7 of them waterfront, sites in the 13-21 block) and 9 ATV-camping sites; accommodates RVs up to ~40 ft. $35 no-hookup / $45 waterview-hookup. 14-day max stay. Season ~May 15-Oct 24. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. Operated by NH Division of Parks & Recreation. --Claude

name: Campton Campground
note: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), off NH-49 ~2 mi from I-93 exit 28. 58 sites among white pines; max RV/trailer 50 ft. No hookups or dump station; coin showers ($2.50). Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable (online/phone) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Waterville Campground
note: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), Waterville Valley. 27 sites total — 6 tent-only (no vehicles), 19 sites fit RVs/trailers ~25–30 ft (30 ft cap); a 23-ft rig fits. No hookups; vault toilets, potable water. Open mid-May to mid-October, ~$24/night. Mix of reservable and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: White Ledge Campground
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District), off NH-16 ~5 mi south of Conway, base of Mt. Chocorua. 28 sites (some tent-only); fits RVs. No hookups or dump station; accessible restrooms, hand-pump water. Open mid-May to mid-October, $30/night. Mix of reservable (online/phone) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Tripoli Road Camping Area
note: WMNF designated roadside/dispersed camping corridor along Tripoli Rd (reached from I-93 exit 31). Drive-in numbered roadside sites managed by a concessionaire; register at the trailer on the western end. Sites range from riverside to secluded wooded; no hookups, no amenities (primitive). Open mid-May through October, FCFS only — no advance reservations; flat per-vehicle fee (~$20 weekday / $25 weekend). Site sizes vary — not all fit a 23-ft rig; choose a pull-through/larger pulloff. --Claude

name: Passaconaway Campground
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District), on the Kancamagus Highway (NH-112) ~14 mi west of Conway. 33 quiet wooded back-in sites suited to vans, truck campers, and smaller RVs/trailers — a 23-ft rig fits some sites but not the largest rigs. No hookups (no Kanc campground has them). Swift River a short distance away. Open mid-May to mid-October, $30/night. FCFS only — no reservations. --Claude

name: Jigger Johnson Campground
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District), on the Kancamagus Highway (NH-112). 75 wooded sites (1–9 tent-only, rest fit RVs/trailers — large sites accommodate most rigs, only road maneuverability limits length). No hookups; the only Kanc campground with (coin) showers, flush toilets. Swift River behind the campground. Open mid-May to mid-October, $30/night. FCFS only — no reservations. --Claude

name: Covered Bridge Campground (WMNF)
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District) campground on Passaconaway Rd off the Kancamagus Hwy (Rt 112), Albany. 49 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water. Most sites max ~25 ft trailer/RV. Reservable on recreation.gov (cg 232171). Season mid-May to mid-Oct. Note: the historic Albany Covered Bridge has a 7'9" height / 3-ton limit, so larger rigs must enter via Passaconaway Rd from West Side Rd in Conway, not over the bridge. --Claude

name: Blackberry Crossing Campground (WMNF)
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District) campground on the Kancamagus Hwy (Rt 112) ~6 mi west of Conway, across from the Albany Covered Bridge. 26 sites, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water; mostly level compacted-gravel pads (some former-CCC concrete pads). Sites fit RVs/trailers well over 23 ft (allstays lists up to ~65 ft; rec.gov site A045 35 ft). First-come, first-served only — NOT on recreation.gov. Season mid-May to mid-Oct; $30/night + $6 extra vehicle. Former 1930s CCC camp with self-guided tour. --Claude

name: Russell Pond Campground
note: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District), near Woodstock off Tripoli Rd. 84 sites (tent to RV); max trailer 40 ft. Flush toilets, hot showers; no on-site dump station. Open mid-May to mid-October. Mix of reservable and FCFS sites (the prime pond-side sites are FCFS-only). --Claude

name: Big Rock Campground (WMNF)
note: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District) campground on the Kancamagus Hwy (Rt 112), ~7 mi east of Lincoln. 28 wooded sites (sites 21-28 tent-only), each with table, tent pad and parking turnout; no hookups, no water/electric/sewer. RVs/motorhomes up to ~40 ft on most sites (8 sites share a common lot). First-come, first-served only — NOT on recreation.gov. Season mid-May to mid-Oct; $30/night + $6 extra vehicle. --Claude

name: Wildwood Campground (WMNF)
note: WMNF (Pemigewasset Ranger District) campground on NH Rt 112 in Easton, ~9 mi west of North Woodstock along the Wild Ammonoosuc River. 26 wooded sites, gravel pads, no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water; CCC picnic pavilion across the road. First-come, first-served (self-service pay) — NOT reservable on recreation.gov. FS lists max equipment length 50 ft; some reviews note tight access for larger trailers due to road/site conditions, so it suits a 23-ft rig more than big rigs. Season ~mid-May to Oct; $24/night + $6 extra vehicle. RV Life rating is low (unrated/1*) but it is a confirmed, currently-operating WMNF campground. --Claude

name: Haystack Road Dispersed Camping (WMNF)
note: DISPERSED drive-in camping corridor on Haystack Rd (Forest Rd off US-3, ~north of the Beaver Brook Picnic Area), Jefferson/Twin Mountain in the WMNF. 11 numbered, wooded drive-in sites, free, first-come-first-served, 14-night limit, up to 3 vehicles/15 people per site. Only amenity is a fire pit — no water, toilets, or trash. Seasonal: road closed in winter, opens late spring after it dries out (mid-June in some years); check the WMNF page/Facebook for status. Road ends at the Little River and the North Twin trailhead. Sites are short/rustic — fine for a 23-ft rig but verify length on arrival; not a reservation campground. --Claude

name: Sugarloaf 2 Campground
note: White Mountain NF (USFS) campground on Zealand Rd off US-302, near Jefferson/Twin Mountain. 32 rustic sites near the Ammonoosuc River; more RV-capable than Sugarloaf 1 (per-site limits ~25-30 ft, e.g. site 18 = 30 ft). No hookups, no dump station; vault toilets, hand-pump potable water. Mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable on recreation.gov (some sites FCFS). $24/night. --Claude

name: Sugarloaf 1 Campground
note: White Mountain NF (USFS) campground on Zealand Rd off US-302, near Twin Mountain. 29 rustic sites, single loop along the Zealand River; skews more tent sites than Sugarloaf 2. No hookups, no dump station; vault toilets, hand-pump potable water. Mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable on recreation.gov (some sites FCFS). $24/night. --Claude

name: Cold River Campground (WMNF)
note: WMNF (Saco Ranger District) campground on Rt 113 at the southern end of Evans Notch, Chatham (~15 mi N of Fryeburg ME), near the Cold River and Basin Pond. 14 sites organized on one loop; no hookups, vault toilets, hand-pump water, picnic pavilion; no showers/dump. Sites accept RVs/trailers up to ~40 ft. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov cg 232175) and FCFS sites. Season ~mid-May to mid-Oct; $30/night + $6 extra vehicle. RV Life unrated (0) but confirmed operating via FS and rec.gov. --Claude

name: Zealand Campground
note: White Mountain NF (USFS) campground on Zealand Rd off US-302 near Twin Mountain. 11 rustic sites in a single loop between the highway and the Ammonoosuc River; small RVs fit but the loop road is tight (no posted max length). No hookups, no dump, no showers; vault toilets, potable water. Mid-May to mid-Oct. FCFS only -- not reservable on recreation.gov. $24/night. --Claude

name: Basin Campground
note: White Mountain NF (USFS) campground in the Evans Notch / Cold River area off NH-113, Chatham. 13 sites (7 standard nonelectric, 6 tent-only); standard sites cap ~30 ft, a 23-ft rig fits but no pull-throughs/not big-rig friendly. No hookups, no dump/showers; vault toilets, potable water. Mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable on recreation.gov. Loop set back from Basin Pond (separate day-use area/boat launch). NOTE: closed for construction, expected reopen mid-2026 -- confirm via recreation.gov or Saco Ranger District before relying. --Claude Rechecked 2026-09-30: open (recreation.gov shows late-September 2026 sites reserved/available). --Claude

name: Dolly Copp Campground
note: Largest WMNF (USFS) campground, ~177 sites in 13 loops on the Peabody River in Pinkham Notch off NH-16, near Gorham. Post-renovation: ~52 sites have water + 30/50-amp electric, rest non-electric, no sewer. Flush toilets, coin showers, potable water. Per-site max length varies (many fit 40-45 ft; 23-ft rig fits easily). Mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS sites. RIVE loop borders the river. $30/night ($14 electric). --Claude

name: Wheelock Park Campground
note: City of Keene Parks & Recreation municipal campground. 43 sites -- mix of full-hookup, water-only, electric-only and no-hookup (dry) sites; big-rig friendly up to ~40 ft. Dump station, swimming pool (fee, late June-Aug), hot showers, laundry, playground, ballfields. Open Memorial Day weekend through mid-September. Reservable online via RecDesk or by phone. RV Life: 0.0* / $ (unrated). --Claude

name: Storrs Pond Recreation Area
note: Owned and operated by the Hanover Improvement Society (private non-profit). 17 RV sites + 12 tent sites; RV sites big-rig friendly up to 50 ft with full or partial hookups; dump station, swimming pool, hot showers, laundry. Season mid-May through Columbus Day. Reservations strongly recommended -- book online at storrspond.org or call the office. RV/site fee around $47/night (4 people). --Claude

name: Wolfeboro Campground
note: Family-owned since 1971; 50 wooded sites (RV sites 1-42 plus tent sites T-1-T-11). RV sites have water/electric/sewer, 20/30-amp, dump station; max trailer length 32 ft. Open ~late May (Memorial Day)-mid Oct (Columbus Day). Both nightly transient (2026 RV $45/night) and seasonal sites; 2-night weekend minimum. Phone reservations only with mailed deposit check, no online booking. Store, laundry, heated restrooms/showers. --Claude

name: Baker River Campground
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: The Baker River half of Modern America's Riverbrook & Baker River in Rumney, on the river, with a beach for swimming, fishing and tubing.  Riverbrook, its sister campground a mile west on Route 25, has the office, and Campspot books both on one listing.  Open from Memorial Day to Columbus Day, for seasonal campers as well as nightly ones. --Claude

name: Riverbend Family Campground
note: Family-owned campground on the Bearcamp River, 11 Jackman Pond Rd, South Tamworth; ~27-35 sites, a mix of seasonal and nightly. Full hookups (water/sewer, 20/30/50-amp) on pull-thrus and back-ins, plus partial-hookup sites for tents, vans and pop-ups; max RV ~45-60 ft. Pool, playground, store, bathhouse, riverwalk. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Book by phone. --Claude

name: The Pastures Campground
note: Privately owned (Doug & Kim Robinson) campground on the Connecticut River at 499 NH Route 10, Orford; NH's only private campground on the Connecticut River. ~61 sites (some listings say 65) on grass, 30/50-amp, water + electric at all sites, sewer/full hookups on some; max RV 43 ft. Mix of seasonal and nightly transient (daily/weekly/seasonal rates; 2026 daily ~$40 RV / $35 tent). Boat dock, canoe/kayak/pontoon rentals, heated pool, public boat launch on adjacent property. Reservations by phone/email; no online booking. Open ~late May-early fall. --Claude

name: Rudy's Cabins and Campground
note: Private RV campground + cabins in the Great North Woods on Clarksville (Rudy's) Pond. 41 sites total: 38 seasonal/long-term, only 3 overnight transient sites (all full hookup, 30/50 amp, ~$60-65/night). Pull-through and back-in gravel sites; RVs to ~50 ft. One waterfront cabin and a few pond-edge tent sites; RV sites set back from water. Open Memorial Day-November. Fly-fishing pond, ATV-trail access. Operator: Rudy's Cabins and Campground, LLC. --Claude

name: Charlestown Breachway Campground
note: RIDEM barrier-beach campground on the east side of the breachway between Ninigret Pond and Block Island Sound. 75 RV-only sites; self-contained units required (no tents, pop-ups, or canvas-top campers; permanent holding tanks). No hookups, no on-site dump/water (use Burlingame or Fishermen's Memorial). Packed-sand parking lot, rough access road but normal-vehicle drive-in (not 4WD); back-in sites 30-40 ft, max 40 ft. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. Open ~April-Oct. --Claude

name: Fishermen's Memorial State Park & Campground
note: RIDEM state campground on the Point Judith peninsula, Narragansett. 182 sites: 147 trailer/RV + 35 tent-only across 4 areas. Areas 1 & 2 full hookups (W/E/S), Area 4 water+electric (no sewer), Area 3 tent-only no utilities. RV sites to 50 ft; a 23-ft rig fits easily. Reservable online via ReserveAmerica. Season ~April 10-Oct 30. --Claude

name: Lake St. George State Park
note: Maine state park campground on Lake St. George near Liberty; Route 3 runs close on the far side of the loops. The official guide caps practical RVs at ~24 ft due to a switchback entrance driveway -- the 23-ft EKKO is fine, larger rigs are limited by the entrance, not the sites. Season mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Crocker Pond Campground

season.note: Mid-May to mid-October.

note: White Mountain NF campground under tall white pines on the edge of Crocker Pond; non-motorized boat launch. Reached by Flat Road from Route 2 in West Bethel: 5.8 mi, then a 0.5-mi dirt road. No length posted, so a 23-ft rig's fit isn't confirmed. --Claude

name: Hastings Campground

season.note: Mid-May to mid-October; Route 113 is gated closed in winter.

season_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/whitemountain/recreation/hastings-campground ('mid-May - mid-October', 'Route 113 is gated closed during the winter months'), read 2026-11-02
note: White Mountain NF campground on Route 113, 3 mi south of Route 2 near Gilead, at the base of Mt. Hastings near Evans Brook; shaded, well-separated sites around a single loop, with a large open play area. --Claude

name: Sleeping Bear Campground & Cabins

season.note: Campground 'Memorial Day weekend through Columbus Day weekend'; cabins open year-round.

note: Small owner-run campground in the Lincoln Lakes region, village of Lee; RV + tent + cabins, wooded, with a wedding and event pavilion. ATV and snowmobile trails from the site; Silver Lake's public beach under a mile away. --Claude

name: South Arm Campground
note: On a peninsula on Lower Richardson Lake (Andover); 65 wooded W/E sites (RVs to 60 ft), about half right on the lake, plus 35 tent sites; sandy beach, 40-slip marina, boat/canoe rentals, store. Open ~late May-late Sept; no cell service. A 2026 camper reports the camp runs on generators, with no power or water 9 pm-7 am. --Claude

name: River Run Canoe & Campground

season.note: 'River Run Is Open Memorial Day Weekend - Labor Day Weekend'.

note: Wooded campground on the Saco River in Brownfield, with 3 private swimming beaches, canoe rentals and a shuttle. Fit for a 23-ft motorhome isn't confirmed: the operator's pages describe wooded sites and don't mention RVs, though AAA lists 58 RV sites. --Claude

name: Oceanfront Camping @ Reach Knolls

season.note: Memorial Day to mid or late October.

season_source: https://reachknolls.com/information.html ('Open from Memorial Day until mid/late October'), read 2026-11-02
note: On Eggemoggin Reach at the mouth of the Benjamin River (Brooklin); large gravel pads, one-way gravel roads, trail to a rocky private beach. Wi-Fi at the office only. In a Google review of 2026 the owner told a large Class A that the roads are too tight for it. --Claude

name: Highlands Riverbend RV Resort and Cabins
note: Riverfront/creekfront RV resort on the Cullasaja River and Ellijay Creek near Franklin; gravel pads with concrete patios, kayak/tube rentals, open-air clubhouse and pavilion, bluegrass on major holiday weekends. Seasonal, ~April-November. --Claude

name: Rose Creek Family Campground

season.note: Season runs from the first weekend in April through the last weekend in October; the 2026 season's last day is November 1.

season_source: https://rosecreekfamilycampground.com/ ('Our season typically runs from the first weekend in April until the last weekend in October. Our last day of operation of 2026 will be November 1st.'), read 2026-10-22
note: Family campground on Rose Creek off NC-181 in Burke County (Morganton), with tent sites, a creek wading beach, a fishing pond, trails and a game room. Most sites are annual seasonal leases (waiting list); a smaller set of RV and tent sites is kept for overnight guests. --Claude

name: New River Campground (Sparta)

season.note: Closed for the 2026 season on October 12, 2026 ('See ya in April 2027!').

season_source: https://www.facebook.com/newrivercampgroundandcanoe/ (post of October 12, 2026: 'We have officially closed for the 2026 camping season... See ya in April 2027!'), read 2026-10-22
note: On the New River just south of the Virginia line (mailing address Independence, VA), with a mile of river frontage; riverbank tent sites, apartments and studios, picnic shelters, and tubing/kayak/canoe trips that end at the campground. Blue Ridge ~2,600 ft. --Claude

name: Winston-Salem Fairgrounds Campground

season.note: Open all year except mid-September to mid-October, when the Carolina Classic Fair uses the grounds. In winter and cold weather, water may be off while facilities are winterized.

season_source: https://wsfairgrounds.com/campground/ ('The RV Campground is available for use throughout the year with the exception of mid-September through mid-October due to the annual Carolina Classic Fair'; '*During winter and cold weather months, water may not be available due to the winterization of facilities.'), read 2026-10-22
note: City of Winston-Salem (Fairgrounds) RV campground at 569 Fairgrounds Blvd, entered at Gate 7; the gate and bathhouse open with a code sent on booking. Not a long-term stay facility. --Claude

name: Ralph J Andrews Recreation Park

season.note: 'Open Seasonally: Spring - Fall' (no dates published). From January 1 to April 1 reservations are taken by phone 9am-3pm only.

season_source: https://www.jacksonnc.org/486/RJA-Campground ('Open Seasonally: Spring - Fall'; 'from January 1st-April 1st reservations will only be taken from 9:00am-3:00pm'), read 2026-10-22
note: Jackson County Parks & Rec campground on Lake Glenville: 6 full-hookup and 18 power-and-water sites (50-amp per the original sweep source) plus primitive and group sites; playground and picnic shelter. --Claude

name: Oconee State Park

season.note: 'During the winter season of Dec.-March, please contact the park for information on winter closures for all campsites.'

note: 20-acre Campground Lake (pier, swim area, boat rentals) + 12-acre lake. --Claude

name: Hiwassee/Ocoee Scenic River State Park - Gee Creek Campground
note: Gee Creek Campground: 47 drive-in sites on A and B loops, concrete pads 40-108 ft (some north-side Loop A sites need leveling). No hookups; potable water pumps, central bathhouse with hot showers, table/fire ring/grill per site. Seasonal (approx Apr 1-Oct 31), reservable online (reserve.tnstateparks.com). NOTE: park announced infrastructure renovation closing the campground fall 2026, reopening anticipated spring 2027. Operator: TN State Parks. --Claude  The reservation calendar now says the campground closes for renovation from early spring 2027 until summer 2028; October 2026 nights are still bookable (read 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Chilhowee Campground
note: USFS Cherokee NF (Ocoee Ranger District) campground atop Chilhowee Mtn. 62 reservable sites across loops A-F: RV electric, RV nonelectric, and tent-only; RV sites accommodate large rigs (electric 55-75 ft, nonelectric up to 80 ft). 30/50-amp electric at electric sites; dump station at end of E Loop; water hydrants throughout; bathhouses with flush toilets/showers. Season ~mid-April to late Oct (overflow/day-use year-round). Reservable online. Access via paved FR 77/Oswald Dome Rd (7.5 mi climb) -- FS warns NOT to follow GPS up the unpaved Benton Springs Rd. 7-acre McKamy Lake offers day-use swim beach and fishing. --Claude

name: Big Oak Cove Campground
note: USFS Cherokee NF, Tellico Plains Ranger District. ~11-12 small primitive sites (gravel pads) on the Tellico River along paved Tellico River Rd (FR210). Picnic table, fire ring, lantern post, vault toilets; NO potable water, NO hookups. RV + tent (small rigs; sibling sites on this road fit ~25-26 ft).
